newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares jump 2.44 pct in continued buying.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares jump 2.44 pct in continued buying.

text.p: Istanbul shares jumped amid rising turnover on Thursday morning as buying continued on the growing expectations of a new secularist alliance to replace the ruling Islamist-led coalition government, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed 35 points, or 2.44 percent higher at 1,472 after easing slightly from a mid-session high of 1,474. Morning volume rose sharply to 10.28 trillion lira from 6.51 trillion on Wednesday.

"The market liked the new government scenario because there was no other political expectation that could fuel purchases. But we cannot say this is an overall buying wave. There will be caution until a possible censure motion," said Hakan Tezcan from Korfez investment.

The index rebounded three percent in the past two days on the rising prospect of a new government after diving 8.9 percent on political jitters to Monday's 1,395 close from April 24 opening which followed a 6-1/2 day holiday.
Brokers await resistance at the index's 1,480 level and then at 1,500.

Former minister Yalim Erez from the conservative True Path Party (DYP) who held a second round of talks with two opposition leaders on Tuesday on forming a secularist pact to exclude the ruling Islamists is expected to discuss his plan soon with deputy Prime Minister and DYP leader Tansu Ciller.
A conservative and a left-wing opposition leader said on Tuesday they fully agreed on the new coalition proposal which Erez said would aim to rule rather than hold early elections.
It is not clear how many DYP deputies will support Erez's move but conservative opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz has said there was support within the party.
Erez has also said the opposition planned to file a censure motion against the government if the DYP did not pull out of the government.

Of the 248 shares traded, rises outdid falls sharply by 149 to 33 and 66 were unchanged. The IMKB Industrial firmed 1.48 percent to 1,442, the IMKB Services leapt 2.53 percent to 1,377 and the IMKB Financial soared 3.24 percent to 1,593.
